These applications coming on for admission this day, the  the following:
 ORDER

These first bail applications under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure have been filed on behalf of applicants for grant of regular bail relating to F.I.R. No. 173/2023 dated 12.5.2023 of Police Station - Junnardev, District Chhindwara (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 363, 366-A, 376(2)(n) and 343 of IPC and under Sections 4, 5L and 6 of POCSO Act, 2012.

Applicants are in detention since 25.5.2023.
2.

As per the prosecution story, on 12.5.2023, prosecutrix's mother lodged an FIR alleging that on 8.5.2023 at around 10 a.m. her daughter left Safdarjung railway station (Delhi) through Patalkot Express for Junnardeo (Chhindwara).
She was having Rs.80,000/- with her.
On 9.5.2023 when train reached at the railway station, she was not found in the train at railway station.
She is missing.
FIR was registered for commission of offence under Section 363 of IPC.
Matter is still under investigation.
3. Learned counsel for applicants have submitted that the applicants have not committed any offence.
They are innocent.
They have been falsely implicated.
They are women and there are no allegation against them that they committed any rape/ aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the prosecutrix.
The only allegation against them is that prosecutrix along with main accused stayed in their house and they did not inform anyone about her presence in the house.
Therefore, it has been prayed that applicants be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail to the applicants.

sentences.text:
5. I have gone through the prosecutrix statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C.
Applicants are ladies and therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicants may be released on bail.
Consequently, these first bail applications are allowed.

6. It is directed that applicants, namely Nasra Bano, Shabnam Bano, Nahid Khan and Fareen Khan be released on bail upon their furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand) each with one solvent surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for their regular appearance before the concerned Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the trial Court during the pendency of trial and will not create any hindrance in progress of trial.
7. It is further directed that the applicants shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the condition of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE mrs. mishra Nasra Bano vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71337462/
